author: PCarme
body:
We are getting a couple of inaccurate mappings to the 2 carbamoyl-phosphate synthase activities [GO:0004087](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0004087) and [GO:0004088](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0004088) to S. pombe genes from RHEA mappings. 

For context, here is the initial discussion about this issue: https://github.com/pombase/curation/issues/3836
CC @ValWood 

It is a pretty long and confusing thread, so I'll try to summarise it here. 

As described in this review (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11212301/) these 2 activities both catalyse the formation of carbamoyl-phosphate via a similar multi-step reaction. The difference between them is that the CPS (ammonia) activity can only use free ammonia as nitrogen donor, while the CPS (glutamine-hydrolyzing) activity has a glutaminase activity which catalyses the release ammonia from glutamine, allowing it to use glutamine as nitrogen donor. 

In yeast, there are 2 CPS enzymes: 
- The mitochondrial CPS complex, which is a heterodimer formed of a large subunit carrying a CPS (ammonia) activity, and a small subunit carrying a glutaminase activity. So, while the whole complex can be described as a glutamine-hydrolyzing CPS, the catalytic subunit's activity is ammonia-specific. In S. pombe, the large subunit is called Arg4 (https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC215.08c), and the small subunit is Arg5 (https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPBC56F2.09c).
- The cytosolic CPS, which is a single multifunctional protein with a CPS (glutamine-hydrolyzing) activity. In S. pombe, this protein is called Ura1 (https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC22G7.06c). 


Now for the actual issue, basically we get 2 inaccurate mappings to CPS activities from RHEA:
- Arg4 / SPBC215.08c gets annotated as a glutamine-hydrolyzing CPS ([GO:0004088](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0004088)) via RHEA:18633, although its actual catalytic activity is ammonia-specific.
- Ura1 / SPAC22G7.06c is annotated as an ammonia-specific CPS ([GO:0004087](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/GTerm?id=GO:0004087)) via RHEA:18029, while it is a glutamine-hydrolyzing CPS. 

Both of these genes already get the correct CPS annotations from another source, so all we need is for the incorrect mappings to be removed.
title: Incorrect RHEA:18633 and RHEA:18029 mappings in S. pombe
